newsitem.title: USA: Coast Guard to set curbs Monday for St Louis port.
newsitem.headline: Coast Guard to set curbs Monday for St Louis port.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard said it will impose navigation restrictions for the port of St Louis on Monday due to high water on the Mississippi River there.

"We have set up a safety zone in the St Louis area which includes River Mile 184, north of St Louis to River Mile 179, south of St Louis," said Lt. Drew Cheney, assistant chief of port operations, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office, St Louis.

The Coast Guard said it will allow barges to pass with some restrictions. All tows must have a minimum of 250 horsepower per 1,500 tonnes cargo, which is a standard loaded barge. Also, southbound tows greater than 600 feet excluding the tow boat may transit the zone during daylight hours only.
"This safety zone will remain in effect until the St Louis river level gauge reading is less than 25 feet," Cheney said.
The Mississippi River at St Louis now stands at 27.6 feet, just under flood stage of 30 feet.
"We are expecting it to crest at about 33 feet on April 18," Cheney said.

River officials said the high level of snow accumulated in the upper Midwest over the winter as well as the rapid spring snow melt in Minnesota and Wisconsin have contributed to high water levels on the tributaries which flow into the upper Mississippi.
"The Mississippi River levels are rising all the way down southward. We still have high water levels up north near the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and St Paul (Minn.)," Cheney said.
He noted as the river flows toward the Gulf of Mexico, water levels were rising in Iowa, Illinois and Missouri areas.
